text:
carla: Quick sync — need to lock acceptance criteria + rollout plan for the "cohort bootstrapping" onboarding lane. customers asking for faster turnups and clearer SLAs.
ben: can you summarize the core asks?
carla: 1) onramp customers (small cohorts) should be able to onboard a model from catalog in <48h. 2) We need a clear perf/cost bar to list a model as "production-ready". 3) special handling for air-gapped / private installs.
devon: perf/cost bar idea: p95 <= 200ms for 512 tokens on hosted, token unit cost delta <= +25% vs baseline, and eval regression <= 3% on our standard prompt set.
emma: +1 on p95. also require observability hooks — token-level cost + latent traces turned on by default for canaries. ops-bot: deploy checklist created: https://redwood.internal/checklists/cohort-bootstrapping (auto-post)
carla: proposal: make two acceptance tiers — "preview" and "production". preview = quick onramp w/ reduced SLOs (48h), prod = locked perf & canary plus rollback gates.
alice: from sales: we need a short customer-facing table that maps tiers -> guarantees -> price delta. customers will pay for faster onboarding.
ben: implementation notes: for prod tier we should require pinned model version + quantization profile pre-validated on the Dedicated infra bucket. preview can use floating variant but flagged.
devon: metric definitions we should track during canary: p50/p95/p99, token cost per 1k, eval-quality delta, unforced fallback rate (model fallbacks), and cache hit ratio.
emma: rollout recipe suggestion: canary cohort = 2% traffic for 72h; health gates: no >2% error spike, p95 < 1.3x baseline, and eval-quality dip < 2.
carla: edge cases: 1) big customers who demand pinning forever — need contract clause and migration path. 2) customers that require airgap -> will be slower and need ops support.
alice: can we offer an "onboarding credit" program for co-marketing? helps adoption for the preview tier.
ben: engineering constraints: validating quantization profiles takes ~1-2 dev-days per model on Dedicated, and we need a small infra job to run nightly stability tests.
devon: question: do we want an automated quality regression check (eval harness) gated before prod listing? I vote yes — prevents obvious breaks.
carla: yes — gate must be automated. define eval harness: 3 benchmark suites: functional, spam/abuse, and latency-sensitive prompts. pass thresholds or create a pin-exception ticket.
emma: SRE ask: include an alarm runbook for canary anomalies and an automated rollback step which triggers a model swap to previous pinned variant.
carla: rollback criteria draft: if any of these happen during canary => auto-rollback: 1) sustained p95 > 2x baseline for >15m, 2) error rate >3%, 3) eval-quality regression >5% on key prompts.
ben: can we make the p95 gate configurable per-customer? enterprise customers may need tighter SLOs.
alice: yes — contracts can list custom SLOs and custom pricing.
carla: timeline: propose we pilot this with 3 models next sprint: 1 small L2 open model, 1 mid-size encoder-decoder, 1 customer-requested quantized variant.
devon: I'll own the eval harness + quality gates. ben owns infra validation and pinning workflow. emma owns canary SLO alarms & rollback runbooks. carla will own docs + customer table.
carla: docs: we need a customer-facing onboarding matrix and an internal playbook (runbook + checklist). ops-bot: created internal ticket RW-PL-987: "Cohort bootstrapping runbook" (link auto-added).
ben: quick note on quotas: preview cohorts should have quota caps to avoid noisy tenants; propose per-customer QPS cap and token cap for first 48h then auto-lift if canary healthy.
eletter: (typo)
alice: marketing: short one-pager + pricing table by EOW? we can push to customers in next wave.
devon: measurement: add a dashboard tile with cohort health score (0-100) combining p95, error rate, and eval-quality. we can use that for go/no-go.
emma: final ask: define a small emergency rollback comms template for CS when a customer's model is rolled back.
carla: agreed. i'll draft the acceptance doc after this thread and share. Action items: Devon: eval harness (owner). Ben: infra validation + pin workflow. Emma: canary alarms/runbook. Alice: customer table + incentives. Carla: draft acceptance + docs.
ben: ok, ping me if you need infra testbed access.
carla: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
